source.title: Kafka Streams in Action, Second Edition — Kafka clients / transactional producer section
source.author: Bill Bejeck

observation: The inspected source describes a transactional Kafka producer that is partitioned from the transaction coordinator, cannot commit, and times out. The coordinator aborts the transaction and advances the producer epoch from 5 to 6. When the network connection returns, the old producer sends epoch 5; the coordinator rejects the request because the epoch no longer matches and the producer is fenced. The source also points to TransactionalProducerConsumerTest.java as an example test for transactional producers.
falsifying_trace: network partition prevents commit/abort from reaching coordinator
transaction timeout causes coordinator to abort and advance epoch to 6
old producer reconnects and attempts transaction completion with epoch 5
coordinator rejects the stale epoch; producer receives fencing failure
exact_scope: This establishes, for the described Kafka transactional-producer protocol, that epoch authority is checked by the transaction coordinator after a communication break and that a stale epoch is rejected. It does not establish a measured two-host topology, an injected real network partition, or a resource-side protected business mutation trace in the cited source.
witness_gap: The source is explanatory text rather than a reported measured two-host experiment. Although it names a transactional producer test, the inspected source does not show that test using two hosts/processes or injecting a network partition, nor does it report before/after mutation values proving a stale holder attempted and failed a protected resource write. Therefore FE-489 does not close the real-multihost/resource-fencing frontier.
negative_result: Protocol documentation-style fencing evidence is insufficient for the requested real two-host measured witness when topology, fault injection, stale mutation attempt, and resource rejection are not all directly observed in the same source.
exact_next_action: Fresh-bootstrap next invocation, persist/read back mandatory preflight, then inspect exactly one official project source that contains an executable or reported multi-process/multi-host fencing test with an injected communication fault or explicit stale-owner takeover. Require all four in the same source: distinct owner identities/topology, authority epoch/token advance, stale mutation attempt, and server/resource rejection or unchanged protected value. Prefer Kafka system/integration tests or another first-party distributed-system test; persist one measured trace or exact witness gap only and do not start a second leaf.
